solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Part, getting dry inside, split (6)

indicators.note: to get something is to receive it, so BIT receives the next letters into itself
inside places SEC within BIT, splitting it after BI

blocks.note: a bit is a part
sec is dry, of wine

annotation.surface: Something dried out in the middle has broken apart.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'split' as a past tense, cracked like dry wood; as the definition it is a verb, and the wordplay itself splits BIT in two.
annotation.definitionFit: Bisect is Latin for cut in two, so a plain synonym for split, used of lines, angles and roads.

entries.clue: Bishop’s keeping top off, displaying muscle (6)

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so BP'S holds ICE within it

blocks.note: BP is an abbreviation for bishop, plus the 'S
to top off a cake is to ice it

annotation.surface: A bishop has taken his hat off and is showing off his arm muscles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Top off' looks like an instruction to drop a first letter, but it is a verb: you top off a cake by icing it.
annotation.definitionFit: The biceps is one particular muscle, the one at the front of the upper arm, so the definition is by class.

entries.clue: Reserve power to maintain speed ultimately being considered (3,6)

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold up or support, so JUICE holds the D inside it
ultimately means in the end, so take the end of speed

blocks.note: a sub is a reserve player
juice is slang for electric power
last letter of speed, held inside JUICE

annotation.surface: Keeping power in reserve to hold a speed steady is under discussion.
annotation.walkthrough: Sub judice is Latin for 'under a judge': a case still before a court, which in Britain limits what may be reported.
annotation.definitionFit: A legal term: a matter sub judice is still before the court, being considered, and so not yet open to comment.

entries.clue: Roughly formulate 29 beliefs (5)

annotation.definitionNote: credo is singular, a set of beliefs

blocks.note: c = circa, roughly
29 across is AFRESH; to formulate afresh is to redo

annotation.surface: Someone sketches out a rough statement of what they believe.
annotation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to 29 across, AFRESH, so 'formulate afresh' means REDO.
annotation.definitionFit: Credo is Latin for 'I believe', the first word of the Creed, so it names a whole set of beliefs at once.

entries.clue: What you are trying to do amid bad working is excused (8)

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so SOLVE goes into the middle of the rearranged BAD
working means in operation, and BAD is operated on until its letters move

blocks.note: the first part of BAD rearranged as ABD

blocks.clueFragment: What you are trying to do
blocks.note: you, the reader, are trying to solve this crossword
the rest of the rearranged BAD

annotation.surface: Someone who was trying their best amid shoddy work is let off.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue talks to the solver directly: what you are doing right now is trying to SOLVE.
annotation.definitionFit: Absolved comes from forgiveness of sins, and has widened to mean released from blame, which is what excused means.

entries.clue: Fresh, round glass full of alcohol following loaf with jam? (6-2-6)

annotation.definitionNote: an adjective phrase describing traffic in a jam

indicators.note: following means coming after, so everything before it in the clue comes after BUM

blocks.note: to loaf about is to bum around
pert = fresh, cheeky
O is round in shape
a bumper is a glass filled to the brim

annotation.surface: A tea table: fresh round bread, a full glass of drink, and a loaf with jam.
annotation.walkthrough: Loaf and jam set up a tea table, but loaf is a verb (BUM) and the jam is a traffic jam, marked by the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: in a traffic jam cars queue so close that each front bumper nearly touches the rear one ahead.

entries.clue: Tinker too much maybe with old uniform I’m handing back? (4,2,3)

blocks.note: over- = too much, as in overdo
to toy with something is to tinker
admits that OVER-TOY is a coined word, one way of saying tinker too much
o = old
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Someone fiddled too much with an old uniform and is now handing it back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tinker too much' gives an invented verb OVER-TOY, flagged by 'maybe'. The definition is what a broadcaster says when passing the microphone back.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from broadcasting and radio: a presenter says 'over to you' as they hand back to a colleague, and the question mark flags the example.

entries.clue: Footballers through the 50s have spread out (5)

indicators.note: something spread out opens a gap, so VIA spreads to let LL into its middle

blocks.note: via = through
L is Roman 50; two of them

annotation.surface: Football players in the 1950s were spread out across the pitch.
annotation.walkthrough: The 50s look like a decade but are two Roman fifties.
annotation.definitionFit: Aston Villa, a Birmingham football club, is usually called just Villa, so its players stand for the club by metonymy.

entries.clue: Drops key in study in front of CID officer (8)

indicators.note: in places the key inside the study, DEN
in front of means before, so DEN with ESC comes before DS

blocks.note: first letter of DEN, a study
the Escape key on a keyboard
rest of DEN
Detective Sergeant, a CID rank

annotation.surface: A detective drops a key in the study.
annotation.walkthrough: The key is a computer key, not one for a lock. CID is the plain-clothes detective branch of British police.
annotation.definitionFit: Drops here is the intransitive verb, as a road or a plane drops, a plain synonym for descends rather than 'lets fall'.

entries.clue: Put off voting for councillor by a small girl and boy (14)

blocks.note: pro = in favour of
Cr is an abbreviation for councillor
as printed
s = small
a girl's name
a boy's name

annotation.surface: A local election is postponed after votes for a councillor, a girl and a boy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put off' reads as 'discouraged', but it is the definition: delayed.
annotation.definitionFit: Put off is past tense here, delayed, and procrastinated is its formal Latin synonym, from cras, tomorrow.

entries.clue: Message has good stuff after chapter leading up to it (9)

indicators.note: after means later in order, so G RAM goes later than C ABLE
to lead is to go first, so the chapter's C goes before ABLE

blocks.note: c = chapter
up to it = able
g = good
to ram is to stuff

annotation.surface: A note says the good material comes after the chapter that builds up to it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Good stuff' looks like one idea but splits into two; 'up to it' means capable, not 'leading up to'.
annotation.definitionFit: A cablegram is a particular kind of message, a telegram sent by undersea cable, so the definition is by class.

entries.clue: Boy or girl needed for tonsillectomy sent back (5)

indicators.note: the letters are needed for the word tonsillectomy, forming part of it
something sent back travels the way it came, so the letters read right to left

blocks.note: letters inside tonSILLEctomy

annotation.surface: A child needed for a tonsil operation is sent home.
annotation.walkthrough: The hospital story hides the name backwards inside the operation.
annotation.definitionFit: Ellis is a given name used for both sexes, so either a boy or a girl may carry it.

entries.clue: Very good, with United when scoring more (3)

blocks.note: pi, short for pious, = very good
U = United, in football team names

annotation.surface: A football team did very well with United scoring more goals.
annotation.walkthrough: The scoring is musical, not football: più is Italian for 'more' in a written score, as in più forte.
annotation.definitionFit: Più is the Italian musical direction for more, used only when writing a score, which 'when scoring' flags.

entries.clue: Put together, men box in front of judge (11)

indicators.note: in front of means before, so OR and CHEST come before RATE

blocks.note: OR = other ranks, soldiers
a chest is a box
to judge is to rate

annotation.surface: Men assembled a box in front of a judge.
annotation.walkthrough: Box and judge sound like a boxing match or a court, but both are plain nouns and verbs.
annotation.definitionFit: To orchestrate is literally to arrange music for an orchestra, and figuratively to put together or organise anything.

entries.clue: Perennial, regularly used rationing is unknown on reflection (6)

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of 'rationing is' is used
a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters are reversed

blocks.note: the even letters of rAtIoNiNg Is
z is an unknown in algebra

annotation.surface: A garden plant is being rationed and nobody knows why.
annotation.walkthrough: 'is' belongs to the fodder, not the link: the regular letters of 'rationing is' supply the final I.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the zinnia is a daisy-like garden flower, and some species are perennial, which the setter leans on.

entries.clue: Unlimited calls with numbers ending in eight (2-7)

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so eight gives T

blocks.note: nos = numbers
last letter of eight
to call someone is to ring them

annotation.surface: A phone plan with free calls to numbers ending in 8.
annotation.walkthrough: The phone-tariff surface fits the answer: a no-strings deal has no conditions attached.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: an offer with no strings attached has no conditions, so it is unlimited in that sense.

entries.clue: Your out-of-date staff eating iodine for gland (7)

indicators.note: what is eaten ends up inside, so ROD takes the I into itself

blocks.note: thy is the archaic form of your
a rod is a staff
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

annotation.surface: Old-fashioned staff taking iodine to treat a gland.
annotation.walkthrough: The medical surface is apt: the thyroid needs iodine to work.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the thyroid is one specific gland, in the neck, which makes hormones controlling metabolism.

entries.clue: Tesla coil specially designed to sway (9)

indicators.note: something specially designed is built anew, so the letters are rebuilt in a new arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: An electrical coil has been built specially so that it swings.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: a Tesla coil produces an oscillating current.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to swing back and forth, oscillate being the scientific word.

entries.clue: English resort’s bias, replacing whiskey with golf! (8)

indicators.note: to replace is to take the place of, so golf's G takes the place of whiskey's W

blocks.note: skewness = bias, lopsidedness
W is whiskey in the NATO alphabet; it comes out
G is golf in the NATO alphabet; it goes in

annotation.surface: An English seaside town is biased, trading whiskey for golf.
annotation.walkthrough: Whiskey and golf are letters, not pastimes.
annotation.definitionFit: Skegness is a traditional seaside holiday town on the Lincolnshire coast, so an example of an English resort.

entries.clue: Sense new time, with king opening parliament (7)

indicators.note: SENSE is made new, rearranged
an opening is a beginning, so the king comes at the start

blocks.note: k = king, in chess
SENSE rearranged
t = time

annotation.surface: A new era is felt as the monarch opens parliament.
annotation.walkthrough: The State Opening of Parliament by the monarch is the picture; the parliament is Israel's.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Knesset is the name of Israel's parliament, from Hebrew for assembly.

entries.clue: Leak fast, in a word, an alternative to this form of fare … ? (6)

annotation.definition: Leak fast, in a word, an alternative to this form of fare … ?

blocks.note: read as a plumbing emergency; meant as one invented word, LEAKFAST

blocks.clueFragment: an alternative to this form of fare … ?
blocks.note: read as a plea for a different menu; meant as a meal whose name is itself a blend of two meal names, the other blend being the invented word before it

annotation.surface: A riddle about a leak that must be fixed fast and a choice of meals.
annotation.walkthrough: Brunch takes BR from breakfast and UNCH from lunch; swap BR and L and the other blend is LEAKFAST. The clue runs on into 22 across.
annotation.definitionFit: Brunch is a portmanteau meal, eaten late morning in place of both breakfast and lunch, so a form of fare.

entries.clue: Outfit that is Henry’s tawdry (6)

blocks.note: kit = outfit
sc. = scilicet, Latin for 'that is to say'
H is the symbol for the henry, a unit of inductance

annotation.surface: Henry's outfit is cheap and garish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'That is' usually gives IE; here it is the rarer SC, from scilicet.
annotation.definitionFit: Kitsch is borrowed from German for gaudy, sentimental trash, and as an adjective it is a near synonym of tawdry.

entries.clue: … relating to which romantics go crazy (11)

annotation.definitionNote: 'which' points back to the fare of 20 across, so the definition means relating to food

indicators.note: something crazy is disordered, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

annotation.surface: Romantic types lose their heads over good food.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue continues 20 across: 'which' is the fare there, so the answer means relating to food.
annotation.definitionFit: Gastronomic comes from Greek gaster, stomach, and describes anything to do with food and eating, the fare of 20 across.

entries.clue: View of crew changing direction by 90 degrees? (5)

indicators.note: a right-angle turn swaps one compass point for the next, so E becomes S

blocks.note: a rowing eight is a crew
E (east) turns 90 degrees clockwise to S (south)

annotation.surface: What a boat's crew sees as it turns a right angle.
annotation.walkthrough: The first letter of EIGHT is also a compass point, east; a quarter turn makes it south.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as nouns: a sight or view is what you see, as in 'a fine sight' or 'a fine view'.

entries.clue: Welcome to visit church with fine arch (5)

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so HI goes inside CE
with means accompanied by, so F comes along at the end

blocks.note: first letter of CE, Church of England
hi is a welcome
rest of CE
f = fine, on pencils

annotation.surface: Visitors are welcomed to a church with a fine arch.
annotation.walkthrough: Arch looks like part of the church building, but it is the adjective in arch-enemy.
annotation.definitionFit: Arch as an adjective means principal, as in arch-rival or archbishop, the same sense as chief.

entries.clue: Blooming band, playing perhaps, certain to go off (3)

indicators.note: to go off is to leave, so SURE leaves LEISURE

blocks.note: playing is one example of leisure
sure = certain; it is taken away

annotation.surface: A band playing music is sure to go off, and blooming well.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blooming band' suggests a musicians' band, but it is a band of flowers.
annotation.definitionFit: A lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers worn round the neck, literally a band that blooms.

entries.clue: A foolish face might have this urge (3,2)

annotation.definition: A foolish face might have this

blocks.clueFragment: A foolish face might have this
blocks.note: an idiom: a face smeared with breakfast looks embarrassed and silly
to egg someone on is to urge them

annotation.surface: Foolish-looking people might have an urge.
annotation.walkthrough: The first definition is an idiom split in half: 'egg on your face' means embarrassment.
annotation.definitionFit: Egg on is both the stuff on a foolish face and a phrasal verb meaning urge, from an Old Norse word for edge.

entries.clue: Comedy in that place, nearly done by four, too short (3,6)

indicators.note: nearly done means not quite finished, so THERE lacks its last letter
by means beside, so IV stands next to THER
short means lacking a bit, so ALSO lacks its last letter

blocks.note: THERE without its last letter
Roman four
ALSO (too) without its last letter

annotation.surface: A comedy is staged there and nearly finished by four, running short.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Too short' looks like one idea but is ALSO clipped.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: The Rivals is Sheridan's 1775 stage comedy, home of Mrs Malaprop.

entries.clue: Some tennis, then a party, in park (3,5)

indicators.note: then means next in sequence, so A and SIDE follow SET

blocks.note: a set is part of a tennis match
as printed
a side is a party in a dispute

annotation.surface: A game of tennis and then a party, held in a park.
annotation.walkthrough: Park looks like the setting of the tennis and the party, but it is the verb, as in parking an idea.
annotation.definitionFit: Park is informal for putting an issue aside to deal with later, the figurative sense of leaving a car, so a synonym of set aside.

entries.clue: Ref has jogged over (6)

indicators.note: to jog something is to jolt it, so the letters are shaken out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters

annotation.surface: A referee has run over to the incident.
annotation.walkthrough: Over looks like the ref's direction of travel, but it is the adverb in 'start over'.
annotation.definitionFit: Over in 'do it over' is a mainly American adverb for again, which afresh also means.
